callPoints: **Record quarter in a hard environment.** Volumes 1.44 mn (+29%), standalone revenue Rs17,244 cr (+37%), EBITDA Rs3,596 cr (+45%), margin 20.9% (+110 bp YoY, +10 bp QoQ), PAT Rs2,983 cr (+42%). Management says supply problems (LPG shortages, West Asia shipping, labour migration, a ransomware attack) cost ~10% of the quarter's volume.

**Costs.** Commodity inflation was ~4.5% of revenue in the quarter (steel +10%, aluminium, platinum and rhodium ~+40%); price rises in April and June covered about half, the weak rupee (Rs94.4 per dollar vs Rs85.6 a year earlier) and cost cuts the rest. Q2 will carry the full inflation, which has spread to electronics, labour, logistics and energy.

**Exports.** Record 732k units and $735 m (40% of revenue); Africa more than doubled (Nigeria ~60% retail share with the Boxer 125 Heavy Duty), Mexico and Brazil strong, 3W exports 100k (+70%). Target: more than 250k units a month from Q2.

**Domestic motorcycles.** Industry +7-8%, all of it above 125cc; Bajaj gained a couple of points of Vahan share in 150cc+ but keeps losing share in 100-125cc, where it says it will 'participate on its own terms'. An all-new 150cc Pulsar and ~10 facelifts by September, two new 125cc brands within FY27.

**EVs.** Electric 2W + 3W were ~30% of domestic revenue at a double-digit EBITDA margin; Chetak +~80% and now EBITDA positive; Chetak capacity 50k a month going to 60k. Capacity for the whole company to rise from 7 mn to 9 mn units a year.

**Subsidiaries.** First full quarter of KTM (its Jan-Mar 2026) in the consolidated accounts; consolidated revenue Rs21,689 cr (+65%), attributable PAT Rs3,226 cr (+46%). BACL: income Rs1,109 cr, PAT Rs227 cr, AUM ~Rs20,000 cr (+70%), ROE >25%.
**Cash.** FCF ~Rs2,300 cr; surplus cash ~Rs21,000 cr at June, then ~Rs10,000 cr paid out in July (Rs150 final dividend + Rs5,633 cr buyback); management expects ~Rs15,000 cr again by March 2027.

bacl.notes: Wholly owned NBFC (incorporated 2021; share capital Rs2,700 cr). AAA-rated by CRISIL, CARE, ICRA and India Ratings (Q3FY26 call). Penetration of Bajaj's domestic retail ~40-45%. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bajaj Auto (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners via tools/authoring/BAJAJ-AUTO.patch.js). Three business lines that sum to reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA: STANDALONE (Bajaj Auto Ltd: motorcycles, Chetak electric scooters, three-wheelers, exports, spares, export incentives and PLI), BACL (Bajaj Auto Credit, the captive lender; EBITDA struck after its finance cost, which the patch moves out of 'Interest' in history too) and KTM, OTHER SUBSIDIARIES & CONSOLIDATION (Bajaj Mobility AG / KTM, consolidated from 18-Nov-2025 with a one-quarter lag, plus Brazil, BAIH BV and eliminations). The standalone revenue path comes from a volume x realisation build in `businessLines`, checked against model revenue in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js. BACL's borrowings are operating debt (its funding), so net cash and treasury income exclude them. Valued like the street: P/E on Sep-28E STANDALONE EPS (post-buyback share count) plus BACL at P/B and the 74.94% BMAG stake at market less a holding discount, all computed in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js and carried into the engine as an implied multiple of consolidated Sep-28E EPS by BAJAJ-AUTO.sotp.js.
assumptions._shareNote: The engine uses the FY26 share count (27.95 cr = profit for owners Rs10,744 cr / EPS Rs384.41). The July-2026 tender buyback (up to 46.94 lakh shares at Rs12,000, Rs5,632.80 cr) cut the count to ~27.48 cr (274.8 mn; MOSL, Anand Rathi and ICICI Direct use 274.8 mn). Engine EPS is therefore ~1.7% below EPS on the post-buyback count; BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js shows both, and the SOTP is per post-buyback share.

assumptions._capexWhy: Consolidated capex Rs879 cr (FY25), Rs694 cr (FY26; standalone ~Rs500 cr, split equally ICE and EV). FY27-29E: standalone ~Rs900-1,000 cr a year for the 7 mn -> 9 mn unit capacity expansion (EV 2W/3W, premium motorcycles, 3W) plus KTM ~EUR100 m a year (EUR73 m in restructuring-year 2025, EUR178-284 m in 2021-2024) plus BACL ~Rs20 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: Consolidated depreciation Rs645 cr in FY26 (KTM for six weeks) and Rs405 cr in Q1FY27 (Rs1,620 cr annualised: standalone Rs118 cr, BACL ~Rs3 cr, KTM and others ~Rs284 cr incl. amortisation of the Rs3,925 cr of KTM brand and technology intangibles recognised at acquisition). Gross block Rs15,919 cr at Mar-26 incl. KTM at fair value. 9.5% of average gross block gives ~Rs1,610 cr in FY27E.

operatingDebt._why: BACL's borrowings in the consolidated balance sheet at Mar-26: secured INR term loans Rs13,133 cr, ECB Rs2,409 cr, NCDs Rs500 cr, accrued interest Rs26 cr (AR FY26 consolidated note 16; financing-segment liabilities Rs16,003 cr, note 44). They fund the loan book, so they are working capital of the lending business, not group debt; KTM's bank loans (~Rs6,230 cr incl. the EUR473 m drawn under the EUR550 m facility), leases and sales-tax deferral stay as debt.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to consolidated cash and investments less non-BACL borrowings: Rs21,069 cr at Mar-26 (cash Rs3,072 cr + investments Rs24,642 cr - borrowings Rs22,713 cr incl. leases + BACL borrowings Rs16,068 cr). 8.1% x Rs21,069 cr = Rs1,707 cr in FY27E, in line with standalone other income of Rs1,532 cr in FY26 and Rs512 cr in Q1FY27 and brokers' Rs1,610-1,820 cr for FY27E. The yield looks high because the base is net of KTM's debt, whose interest is charged separately below (engine workaround, as for ASIANPAINT).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income of the subsidiaries: consolidated other income exceeded standalone by Rs176 cr in Q1FY27 (KTM, Brazil, BAIH BV interest after KTM repaid its loans in Feb-2026). FY26 reported other income was Rs2,182 cr plus Rs561 cr share of KTM as an associate (incl. Rs1,599 cr one-off remeasurement and currency-reserve gains) less Rs39 cr exceptional items; BAIH BV's interest on its loans to KTM stopped when KTM refinanced in Feb-2026. Consolidated FY27E other income ~Rs2,100 cr vs Rs2,146 cr in FY26 before the associate and exceptional items.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (KTM bank debt, leases; BACL's funding cost is in EBITDA)
assumptions._interestWhy: Consolidated finance cost Rs1,169 cr in FY26, of which BACL Rs908 cr (moved into BACL's EBITDA) and Rs261 cr other; Q1FY27 Rs387 cr of which BACL ~Rs305 cr, leaving Rs82 cr (~Rs330 cr a year): KTM's EUR473 m drawn at EURIBOR+1.40% after the Feb-2026 refinancing, other KTM loans, leases. Falls as KTM repays from Jun-2027.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT Rs4,423 cr, attributable profit Rs3,226 cr -> 27.1% (tax 27.9% less a Rs37 cr minority share of KTM's loss). Standalone and BACL pay ~25.2%; KTM's losses carry little tax credit, and as KTM turns profitable the minorities take 25% of its profit. 26.5% / 26.0% / 25.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Cash returned to shareholders, incl. buybacks, as % of the year's profit (engine workaround: the engine pays out of the same year's profit). FY27: Rs9,825 cr paid in July 2026 = 100% of FY26 standalone profit (final dividend Rs150 a share, Rs4,192 cr, plus a Rs5,633 cr tender buyback at Rs12,000), ~75% of our FY27E profit. FY28-29E 65%: Bajaj paid 70-90% of standalone profit in FY21-23 and 66-72% in FY25 (MOSL models 64-66%).

dcf._betaWhy: Two- and three-wheelers are cyclical and half the business is exported to emerging markets with volatile currencies; net cash and a strong balance sheet offset: beta 0.9, cost of equity 11.9%.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; two-wheeler demand is maturing in India (motorcycles grew ~4% a year over FY19-26) while exports and EVs add growth. 5.5%, the middle of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% over 15 years: ~4-5% volume plus ~3-4% price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~19.5% in FY29E (standalone 20.7%, BACL after funding cost, KTM ~11%) faded to 19%: competition in EVs and the end of PLI and currency tailwinds.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~1.9% to 2% of revenue (maintenance plus regular capacity).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Exports run at 250k+ a month and Nigeria and LatAm keep growing; the Pulsar refresh and two new 125cc brands win back domestic share; Chetak capacity unlocks and EVs stay at double-digit margins; standalone margin ~21.5%; KTM's turnaround reaches low-teens margins by FY29.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: An export market hits a currency crisis again (as Nigeria did in 2023-24), the rupee strengthens and commodity inflation persists; domestic share keeps slipping in the 100-125cc segments; standalone margin falls to ~19%; BACL's credit costs rise; KTM stalls near break-even.

sotp._why: Inputs for the SOTP in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js. Core: standalone EPS (post-buyback count) x the derived P/E (own forward median on standalone EPS x the auto-sector de-rating), Sep-28E. BACL: peers' median P/B at 30-Sep-2026 (CHOLAFIN, SHRIRAMFIN, M&MFIN) on BACL's book at Sep-27E (the target date). KTM: 74.94% of Bajaj Mobility AG's market value on 30-Sep-2026 (EUR31.75, Vienna close; 33.797 mn shares; EUR/INR 109.19, FBIL 24-Sep-2026) less a holding discount (Anand Rathi uses 20%).

cover.headline: A world-class exporter priced for more than its own history says it is worth; KTM and the lender are extras, not the story
cover.lead: Bajaj Auto is India's most profitable two- and three-wheeler maker and its largest vehicle exporter: 5.1 mn vehicles in FY26, 44% of them shipped to 70+ countries, at a 20.5% standalone EBITDA margin. Q1FY27 was a record (volumes +29%, standalone EBITDA +45%) as exports boomed (+54%), the rupee fell to ₹94 per dollar and electric scooters and three-wheelers reached 30% of domestic revenue. But domestic motorcycle share keeps slipping (18.2% in FY24, 15.6% in FY26), and the group now also owns a captive lender (Bajaj Auto Credit, AUM ~₹20,000 cr) and 74.94% of KTM's loss-making parent. The street values Bajaj on **P/E on FY28E/Sep-28E standalone EPS at 23-25x**, some adding KTM and the lender. We do the same, but our derived multiple is **18x** (its own 19.4x median forward P/E since 2021, cut by the sector's 6.9% de-rating): 18x × Sep-28E standalone EPS of ₹514.9 = ₹9,268, plus BACL at 2.8x book (₹506) and the KTM stake at market less 20% (₹256) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹10,885, DCF ₹11,962. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Exports were 2.25 mn units and $2.25 bn in FY26 (+20%) and 12.7 lakh units in Apr-Aug 2026 (+50%). Bajaj is #1 in 9 of 15 key motorcycle export markets, holds ~60% of Nigeria at retail and grows ~2x its top-30 markets. This is a real moat. It is also the most volatile part of the business: Nigeria fell from 50,000 bikes a month to under 5,000 in 2023-24.

arguments.h: At home, a premium and EV story with a shrinking commuter base
arguments.p: Bajaj gives up share in 100-125cc commuters "on its own terms" and wins in 150cc+, KTM/Triumph (1.30 lakh units in FY26) and EVs (Chetak 20.7% share and EBITDA positive; #1 in e-3W). The mix lifts margins; the share loss (2W Vahan share −60 bp YoY in Q1FY27) caps volume. The festive Pulsar relaunch is the test.

arguments.h: Margins: great, but helped by things that can reverse
arguments.p: Standalone EBITDA margin 20.9% in Q1FY27 despite commodity inflation of ~4.5% of revenue. The cushions: a rupee that weakened ~10% in a year, PLI incentives of ₹1,040 cr (~9% of FY26 EBITDA) and price rises. We model 20.6% / 20.7% / 20.7% (FY27-29E), slightly below the street.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street pays for a re-rating
arguments.p: At ₹10,874 the stock trades at 21.1x Sep-28E standalone EPS (~19.6x after taking out BACL and KTM), against a 19.4x median since 2021. Our EPS is in line with the street (FY28E ₹489.5 vs ~₹498.2); the gap is the multiple: 23-25x assumes the 2024 peak multiple is the new normal.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much of the broader cost inflation management warned about hits the margin, and whether the rupee keeps offsetting it.
Festive season (Oct-Nov 2026) and the Pulsar relaunch: an all-new 150cc Pulsar and ~10 facelifts by September, two new 125cc brands within FY27. Domestic share (Vahan) is the number to watch.
Exports: management targets 250k+ units a month from Q2 (Aug-2026: 280k incl. 3W). Nigeria's pre-election buying could fade after the 2027 elections.
KTM: Bajaj Mobility returned to positive EBIT in Q2 2026 (EUR1.3 m); H2 2026 results and covenant tests from Jun-2027 (net debt/EBITDA ≤4.5x).
Capacity from 7 mn to 9 mn units a year and Chetak from 50k to 60k a month: supply has been the constraint in EVs and exports.

blocks.p: Bajaj Auto makes two- and three-wheelers in India: Waluj (2.7 mn motorcycles and 1.02 mn three-wheelers a year), Pantnagar (1.8 mn), Chakan 1 (0.9 mn Pulsar, Dominar), Chakan 2 (0.3 mn KTM, Husqvarna, Triumph) and Chakan/Akurdi (0.48 mn Chetak scooters): 7.2 mn units of capacity at Mar-26 (AR Table 5). In FY26 it sold **51,17,667 vehicles**: 23,49,040 two-wheelers in India (of which 20,43,316 motorcycles and 3,02,674 Chetak electric scooters), 5,18,444 three-wheelers in India, and 22,50,183 vehicles abroad. Its brands span commuters (Platina, CT, the Freedom CNG bike), the Pulsar and Dominar sports range, KTM and Husqvarna bikes it builds for KTM, Triumph's 350-400cc bikes it builds and sells under licence, Chetak scooters, and passenger and goods three-wheelers (petrol, CNG and electric under Wego and Riki). Two big subsidiaries sit around it. **Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL)** lends to buyers of Bajaj vehicles: AUM ~₹18,835 cr at Mar-26, income ₹3,246 cr and profit ₹665 cr in FY26. **KTM**: since 18-Nov-2025 Bajaj owns 74.94% of Bajaj Mobility AG (formerly PIERER Mobility), the listed Austrian parent of KTM AG (KTM, Husqvarna, GASGAS); it had revenue of €1,009 m in 2025 after a restructuring, and €701 m in H1 2026. Smaller pieces: a Brazil plant and sales company (~32,000 bikes in CY2025), and an EV and design subsidiary (Bajaj Auto Technology).

sections.title: A slow-growing domestic market that is splitting in two, and a booming export market that busts every few years

blocks.p: India sold 1,30,64,789 motorcycles in FY26 (+6.6%), the most since FY19 (AR, SIAM data). That is still only ~4% a year of growth over the last decade: a mature, replacement-led market. Inside it the market is K-shaped. Bikes above 150cc grew 20%+ in Q1FY27 while 100-125cc commuters grew in low single digits; the 100cc share of motorcycles has fallen from ~55% to ~46% in 5-7 years (management). Scooters are going electric fast: e-scooters reached ~25% of scooters by Q1FY27. Three-wheelers are going electric even faster: e-autos were 44% of the L5 segment in Q1FY27.

Exports are a different world. India ships two- and three-wheelers mainly to Africa, Latin America and South Asia, where demand swings with oil prices, elections and currencies. FY23-24 were a bust (Nigeria's naira devaluation and inflation cut Bajaj's sales there from ~50,000 a month to under 5,000); FY26 and FY27 so far are a boom (India's motorcycle exports +10% in FY26, three-wheeler exports +44%).

bullets: **Share loss is real.** Bajaj's share of domestic motorcycles was 18.2% in FY24, 16.6% in FY25 and 15.6% in FY26 while the market grew 13.9%, 5.1% and 6.6%. Its own sales: 2.12 mn, 2.03 mn, 2.04 mn. Management says it will participate in 100cc "on its own terms" and favour profit over share; the 100cc segment has shrunk from ~55% to ~46% of motorcycles.

**Premium is where it wins.** 125cc+ is 77.5% of Bajaj's motorcycles. Pulsar passed ₹11,000 cr of domestic revenue in FY26 (₹16,500 cr globally); N and NS series are ~60% of its 150cc+ sales and gained "a couple of points" of Vahan share in five months. KTM and Triumph sold 1.30 lakh bikes in India in FY26 and ~40,000 in Q1FY27 (+50%). The festive relaunch: an all-new 150cc Pulsar and ~10 facelifts by September, then a new 125cc Pulsar and two new 125cc brands within FY27.

**GST.** The Sep-2025 cut (28% to 18% up to 350cc) boosted H2FY26; bikes above 350cc went to 40% and Bajaj absorbed much of it on KTM/Triumph and launched 350cc versions. Price rises from April 2026 handed back 30-40% of the GST benefit (management).

**Chetak** sold 3,02,674 scooters in FY26 (+16%; rare-earth magnet shortages cut H1) with 20.7% of e-scooters, crossed 1 lakh retail in Q4FY26, grew ~80% in Q1FY27 and turned EBITDA positive. Capacity is the limit: 50k a month, going to 60k; exclusive stores 530+ (target ~1,000). EV 2W+3W were ~30% of domestic revenue in Q1FY27 at a double-digit EBITDA margin.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model domestic two-wheelers +6.9% in FY27E (Apr-Aug +12%, Sep-Mar +4% on a GST-boosted base), +7% in FY28E and +6% in FY29E: Chetak and premium grow fast, commuters stay soft. We do not assume Bajaj regains its FY24 share. The risk to us is that the new brands work and share recovers; the risk to the street is that commuter share keeps falling.

bullets: **Scale and reach.** FY26 exports: 22,50,183 units (+20.8%), $2,253 m, ₹20,416 cr. #1 in 9 of 15 key motorcycle markets and 11 of 12 three-wheeler markets; exports passed 2 lakh a month in Oct-2025 for the first time in 39 months. Q1FY27: a record 7.32 lakh units and $735 m (40% of revenue).

**Where.** Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, where Bajaj has a plant making ~32,000 bikes a year and is #5) had its best year; Africa more than doubled in Q1FY27 (Nigeria ~60% retail share with the Boxer 125 Heavy Duty, helped by pre-election institutional buying); Asia was muted (Bangladesh, Nepal); the Middle East was hit by the conflict. India-made KTM exports revived to ~17,500 in Q4FY26 from nearly nil.

**Why it can bust.** Nigeria was a quarter of exports before 2023; its devaluation and inflation took Bajaj's monthly sales there from ~50,000 to under 5,000 (Business Today, Jul-2024) and export 2W fell 25% in FY23 and 10% in FY24. Bajaj's response was to widen the base, so FY26 exports ex-Nigeria were at a record.
**Currency.** Exports are invoiced in dollars: the realised rate rose from ₹85.6 (Q1FY26) to ₹94.4 (Q1FY27). That alone is worth ~10% on 40% of revenue, which explains most of the margin resilience.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** exports of 29,81,643 units in FY27E (+32.5%: Apr-Aug actual +50%, Sep-Mar +22%), $3,015 m at ₹97.2 per export dollar; +10% and +8% in volume after that. This is where we, the street and management are most bullish, and where a single currency crisis would hurt most.

bullets: **What it is.** A wholly owned NBFC started to finance Bajaj's own customers; 65-75% of Indian two- and three-wheelers are bought on credit. ~1.8 mn customers, ~6,200 outlets, penetration ~40-45% of Bajaj's retail. AAA-rated.
**Returns.** ROE ~23% in FY26 and >25% in Q1FY27; GNPA 1.85%, NNPA 1.0%; capital adequacy 19.5% (Tier 1 16.6%). Low operating cost because it is digital and sits inside the dealer network.

**The catch.** Credit cost was ₹543 cr in FY26, ~3.9% of average loans: a high-yield, high-loss book that has not been through a downturn. AUM grows ~70% a year, so the book is unseasoned. Its ₹16,000 cr of borrowings sit in Bajaj's consolidated balance sheet.

blocks.callout: **How we treat it:** BACL's funding cost is part of its EBITDA (patch), its borrowings are operating debt, and in the valuation we take its profit out of the P/E and value it on book instead: 2.8x Sep-27E book of ₹4,967 cr, the median P/B of listed vehicle financiers (Cholamandalam 4.7x, Shriram 2.8x, M&M Financial 1.7x) at 30-Sep-2026. That is ₹506 a share, ~5% of our target.

sections.title: KTM: Bajaj bought control of a broken company cheaply; the turnaround has started but is not yet profitable

blocks.p: Bajaj has owned part of KTM since 2007 and builds KTM's small bikes in Chakan. In 2024 KTM's parent ran out of cash after over-producing into a falling market: revenue fell from €2,661 m (2023) to €1,879 m and it lost €1,080 m. KTM AG went through court-supervised restructuring; production stopped until the end of July 2025. Bajaj arranged an €880 m equity-and-debt package to pay the creditors' cash quota and restart the plants, then exercised call options on the founder's stake. Since 18-Nov-2025 BAIH BV owns 100% of Bajaj Auto International Holdings AG, which owns 74.94% of Bajaj Mobility AG (listed in Zurich and Vienna), which owns KTM AG. In Feb-2026 KTM AG refinanced €550 m with four international banks and repaid Bajaj's loans.

**In Bajaj's accounts.** Six weeks of KTM cost Bajaj ₹872 cr before tax in Q4FY26 (minorities took ₹170 cr), offset by ₹1,599 cr of one-off accounting gains on taking control. blocks.callout: **How we value it:** like the street, separately and at market. Bajaj's 74.94% of Bajaj Mobility was worth ₹8,780 cr at the 30-Sep-2026 close (€31.75 x 33.797 mn shares, ~₹109.19 per euro); less a 20% holding discount (thin free float, no plan to sell; Anand Rathi uses 20%) that is ₹7,024 cr or ₹256 a share, ~3% of our target. KTM's profit is NOT in the standalone EPS we value on P/E, so there is no double count. The market price already assumes a turnaround (EV ~€1.9 bn, ~1.4x 2026 revenue at H1 run-rate); Bajaj's own fair value at acquisition implied ~₹7,880 cr for 100% of the holding company.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a genuine export and three-wheeler moat; none in commuter bikes

verdicts: #1 in 9 of 15 key motorcycle export markets and 11 of 12 3W markets; ~50-60% retail share in Nigeria through ~800 own-brand stores; India's largest 2W exporter ($2.25 bn in FY26).
Hard to copy: decades of distribution, financing and service in Africa and LatAm.
73.8% of ICE 3Ws (87.9% of CNG); #1 in e-3W L5 at 33.5% within three years.
The EV shift lowers its share from three-quarters to one-third of the new segment; still the leader.
Pulsar (₹16,500 cr global revenue), Dominar, KTM and Triumph made in Chakan; KTM-Triumph 1.30 lakh domestic units in FY26; 125cc+ is 77.5% of its motorcycles.
Four brands in 125-400cc give pricing power above the commuter segment.
Share of domestic motorcycles fell from 18.2% (FY24) to 15.6% (FY26); management concedes the 100-125cc segments.
No moat here; Hero, Honda and TVS are stronger.
Standalone EBITDA margin 20.5% in FY26 and 20.9% in Q1FY27, the best among Indian 2W makers; spares ~₹7,000 cr a year at record margins.
Scale in exports and 3Ws plus R&D-led design keep costs low.
Chetak ~20-24% share, EBITDA positive, but demand exceeds its 50-60k a month capacity; TVS, Ather and others compete hard.
A real business now, but no structural edge over TVS.
AUM ~₹20,000 cr, ROE >25%, 40-45% penetration of Bajaj sales.
Supports sales; a young book (credit cost ~3.9%) not yet tested in a downturn.
Iconic premium brands and 29 motorsport titles in 2025, but two years of losses, EUR827 m net debt and EBIT just positive in Q2 2026.
An option on a turnaround, not yet a moat that earns money.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Bajaj has two real moats. In emerging-market exports it has built distribution, brands (Boxer, Pulsar) and service that Chinese and Indian rivals have not matched in thirty years; in three-wheelers it owns three-quarters of the ICE market. Its cost and R&D discipline give it the best margins in the industry. But it has **no moat in the Indian commuter market** (share down 2.6 points in two years), EVs are a fight it is doing well in rather than one it owns, and KTM is a turnaround, not an advantage. A franchise this good deserves a premium to the auto sector; it does not deserve to be priced as if every engine keeps firing at once.

sections.title: Five years of 17% EPS growth in the core business; the group accounts got messier in FY26

blocks.p: Bajaj Auto the company (standalone) grew revenue from ₹27,741 cr in FY21 to ₹58,732 cr in FY26, about 16% a year, and EPS from ₹157 to ₹352, about 17% a year. EBITDA margin rose from 17.8% to 20.5%: exports recovered, three-wheelers and premium bikes grew faster than commuters, and the rupee weakened. The consolidated accounts tell a noisier story because of KTM. In FY25 Bajaj booked a ₹915 cr loss as its share of KTM's collapse (EPS fell to ₹262 from ₹276). In FY26 it booked ₹1,599 cr of one-off accounting gains when it took control of KTM, partly offset by KTM's losses (EPS ₹384). Strip out KTM and the two lines move together.

sections.title: Asset-light at home, capital-heavy outside: ROCE fell from the 30s to 28% as cash went to KTM and BACL

blocks.p: Bajaj's own factories need little capital: standalone capex was ~₹500 cr in FY26, under 1% of revenue, and working capital is negative because suppliers are paid after dealers pay Bajaj. Group ROCE (Screener) was 34% in FY24 and 28% in FY25-26 because money went elsewhere: ₹2,300 cr into BAIH BV (for KTM) and BACL in FY26 alone, and the consolidated balance sheet now includes BACL's ₹18,450 cr loan book and KTM's plants and brands. Consolidated cash from operations was negative in FY25 (−₹1,406 cr) and only ₹2,597 cr in FY26 because BACL's loan growth runs through operating cash flow; standalone free cash flow was more than ₹8,000 cr in FY26 (CFO).

sections.title: Earnings quality: a clean core, but incentives, currency and KTM accounting need watching

bullets: **Incentives are a growing slice of profit.** Government incentives (PLI and state PSI) were ₹1,040 cr in FY26, up from ₹527 cr, and export incentives ₹572 cr; together ~13% of standalone EBITDA, booked as revenue. PLI is time-bound.
**Currency.** Realised USD/INR rose ~10% in a year; with exports ~40% of revenue, that is the main reason margins held through 4.5% commodity inflation. It is earned, but it is not repeatable.

**KTM accounting.** FY25 includes a ₹915 cr share of KTM's loss; FY26 includes ₹1,599 cr of one-off gains (remeasuring the 49.9% stake to fair value and recycling the currency reserve) and KTM's loss for six weeks. KTM is consolidated one quarter in arrears, and Bajaj's Ind AS numbers for KTM differ from Bajaj Mobility's IFRS reports. A ₹21.8 cr bargain-purchase gain went to equity.

**Consolidated cash flow mixes in a lender.** BACL's loan growth is an operating outflow: consolidated CFO was −₹1,406 cr in FY25 and ₹2,597 cr in FY26 against profit of ₹7,325 cr and ₹10,744 cr. Standalone cash conversion is strong (FCF ~80% of PAT in Q1FY27; >₹8,000 cr in FY26).
**Other income** (₹2,668 cr in FY26 on our basis) is 19% of pre-tax profit: treasury income on ~₹20,000 cr of surplus funds plus the KTM items above.
**Disclosure.** Good on volumes and exports; no product-level revenue or margin (motorcycles vs 3W vs EV vs spares). The EV margin is given only as "double digit".

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unmodified audit (S R B C & Co LLP; key audit matters: the KTM business combination and BACL's expected credit loss). The core accounts are clean and cash-backed; the flag is for the group layer: KTM purchase accounting and lag, a fast-growing lender inside the consolidated cash flow, and incentive income.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹21,000 cr outside the lender; borrowings are BACL's and KTM's

blocks.p: Screener shows consolidated borrowings of ₹22,713 cr at Mar-2026, up from ₹124 cr in FY23. None of it is Bajaj Auto's own debt (standalone borrowings ₹73 cr, a sales-tax deferral). About ₹16,068 cr is BACL's funding (bank loans, ECBs, NCDs) against its ₹18,450 cr loan book, and ~₹6,230 cr is KTM's (mainly the €473 m drawn under the €550 m refinancing of Feb-2026), plus ₹659 cr of leases. Cash and investments were ₹27,714 cr. Excluding BACL's borrowings, which fund its loans, net cash was about ₹21,000 cr. Inventory days jumped to 54 in FY26 because KTM's inventory came into the group.

**Biggest swing factor:** the multiple. Each turn on the core is ~₹515 a share; the street's 23-25x versus our 18x is ₹2,574-3,604 a share.

head: Term
What it means
rows: Standalone = Bajaj Auto Ltd on its own (the vehicle business, incl. exports and spares). Consolidated = the group incl. BACL, KTM (since Nov-2025), Brazil and other subsidiaries.
Two-wheelers (motorcycles, scooters); three-wheelers (auto-rickshaws and small goods carriers, which Bajaj reports as "commercial vehicles").
Internal-combustion engine / electric vehicle; L5 = electric autos (higher speed), L3 = e-rickshaws (low speed).
Vahan = government vehicle registrations (retail); wholesale = factory dispatches to dealers, which is what Bajaj reports monthly.
Revenue per vehicle sold. Export realisation depends on the dollar price and the rupee-dollar rate.
Goods and Services Tax; cut from 28% to 18% on motorcycles up to 350cc on 22-Sep-2025, raised to 40% above 350cc.
Production-Linked Incentive (central government scheme rewarding advanced-technology vehicles such as EVs) / Package Scheme of Incentives (state government).
Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd, the captive non-bank lender; AUM = loans outstanding.
Bajaj Mobility AG (formerly PIERER Mobility), KTM's listed parent; BAIH BV (Netherlands) and Bajaj Auto International Holdings AG are Bajaj's holding companies for it.
The ~25% of Bajaj Mobility owned by others; they share its losses and profits, so Bajaj's attributable profit differs from the consolidated total.
When Bajaj took control of KTM it had to revalue its old 49.9% stake to fair value; the gain (₹953 cr) is an accounting entry, not cash.
Price ÷ earnings per share; enterprise value (market value less net cash) ÷ EBITDA; price ÷ book value per share.
Sum of the parts: each business valued separately and added up.
Half FY28E plus half FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
A discount to the market value of a listed stake for illiquidity and the fact that the parent does not intend to sell.

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 10.8% a year over 10 years (5y: 17.8%, 3y: 19.9%), from ₹22,574 cr to ₹62,905 cr.
Profit grew 10.2% a year over the same decade — in line with revenue, i.e. flat margins.
Worst profit year: FY21 (-6.8%); best: FY26 (+46.7%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 15.9%–21.2% since FY15 (peak FY16, trough FY22); FY26 was 19.4%.
Q1FY27 operating margin of 20.9% is lower than 16.3% of the 49 quarters on record — near the top of its history.
Raw-material cost moved from 69% to 67% of sales in FY26 (-2 pts) — the single biggest swing factor in the cost base.
Other income (largely treasury yield on the cash pile) made up 19.1% of pre-tax profit in FY26; reported profit flatters core operations.

returns.text: ROE was 29.0% in FY26 (range 19.9–32.3% since FY15).

DuPont FY26: net margin 17.1% × asset turnover 1.0x × leverage 1.8x.

balance.text: Net cash of ₹5,001 cr (cash + investments less borrowings), 12.9% of net worth.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹40,079 cr of operating cash flow (58.6% of reported profit), spent ₹5,705 cr on capex and paid ₹33,160 cr in dividends.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bajaj Auto (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners via tools/authoring/BAJAJ-AUTO.patch.js). Three business lines that sum to reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA: STANDALONE (Bajaj Auto Ltd: motorcycles, Chetak electric scooters, three-wheelers, exports, spares, export incentives and PLI), BACL (Bajaj Auto Credit, the captive lender; EBITDA struck after its finance cost, which the patch moves out of 'Interest' in history too) and KTM, OTHER SUBSIDIARIES & CONSOLIDATION (Bajaj Mobility AG / KTM, consolidated from 18-Nov-2025 with a one-quarter lag, plus Brazil, BAIH BV and eliminations). The standalone revenue path comes from a volume x realisation build in `businessLines`, checked against model revenue in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js. BACL's borrowings are operating debt (its funding), so net cash and treasury income exclude them. Valued like the street: P/E on Sep-28E STANDALONE EPS (post-buyback share count) plus BACL at P/B and the 74.94% BMAG stake at market less a holding discount, all computed in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js and carried into the engine as an implied multiple of consolidated Sep-28E EPS by BAJAJ-AUTO.sotp.js.
assumptions._shareNote: The engine uses the FY26 share count (27.95 cr = profit for owners Rs10,744 cr / EPS Rs384.41). The July-2026 tender buyback (up to 46.94 lakh shares at Rs12,000, Rs5,632.80 cr) cut the count to ~27.48 cr (274.8 mn; MOSL, Anand Rathi and ICICI Direct use 274.8 mn). Engine EPS is therefore ~1.7% below EPS on the post-buyback count; BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js shows both, and the SOTP is per post-buyback share.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto standalone (vehicles, spares, incentives)
segments._why: From the volume x realisation build in businessLines: FY27E volumes 6.07 mn (+18.5%): Apr-Aug 2026 actual 24.49 lakh (+29%: domestic 2W +12%, export 2W +50%, domestic 3W +15%, export 3W +50%) plus Sep-Mar at domestic 2W +4% (a GST-boosted base from Oct-2025), export 2W +22% (management targets 250k a month; Aug-26 242k), domestic 3W +8%, export 3W +22%. Domestic realisation +5% (price rises in Apr and Jun 2026 recovering ~half of 4.5% commodity inflation, EVs and premium bikes in the mix; Q1FY27 domestic realisation ~+8% YoY), export dollar realisation +1% and the rupee at Rs97.2 per export dollar (FY26 Rs90.6 on AR figures; realised USD/INR 94.4 in Q1FY27 vs 85.6 a year earlier). FY28E: volumes +8.5% (domestic 2W +7% on the Pulsar and new-brand launch cycle, exports +10%); FY29E +7%.
segments._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin 20.2% (FY25), 20.5% (FY26), 20.9% in Q1FY27 despite commodity inflation of ~4.5% of revenue, offset by price, the weak rupee, mix and cost cuts. Management warned that Q2 carries the full inflation (electronics, labour, logistics too). We model 20.6% / 20.7% / 20.7%: EVs at double-digit margins and premium bikes help, but the rupee tailwind cannot keep growing and PLI income (Rs1,040 cr in FY26, ~9% of EBITDA) is time-bound. Brokers model 20.7-21.0% for FY27E.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto Credit (captive lender)
segments._why: Total income Rs1,041 cr (FY25), Rs3,246 cr (FY26), Rs1,109 cr in Q1FY27 (+84%). AUM ~Rs18,835 cr at Mar-26 (doubled) and ~Rs20,000 cr at Jun-26 (+70%). We assume AUM grows ~38% in FY27, ~27% in FY28 and ~21% in FY29 as penetration of Bajaj's retail (45% in Q3FY26) matures and the e-3W and e-rickshaw book grows; income +55% / +30% / +24% (FY27 also carries the full-year effect of FY26's loan growth).
segments._marginWhy: PBT before depreciation as % of income (after finance cost and credit cost): 8.0% (FY25, start-up), 28.0% (FY26), 27.6% (Q1FY27). Credit cost was high (impairment Rs543 cr in FY26, ~3.9% of average loans) and funding costs rise as the book grows faster than equity: 26% / 25.5% / 25%. Implies PAT of ~Rs970 / 1,240 / 1,500 cr and ROE ~25% falling to ~24%.

segments.name: KTM, other subsidiaries & consolidation
segments._why: Consolidated less standalone less BACL. FY26 (Rs927 cr) holds only six weeks of KTM (18-Nov to 31-Dec-2025: Rs1,296 cr of revenue, AR note 46) less eliminations. Q1FY27 (KTM's Jan-Mar 2026) was Rs3,336 cr. FY27E Rs14,000 cr = calendar-2026 KTM: Bajaj Mobility's revenue was EUR331 m in Q1 and EUR370 m in Q2 2026 (+65% in H1); we assume ~EUR1.35-1.40 bn for the year at ~Rs105-108 per euro, less eliminations of Bajaj's sales of India-made KTMs to KTM AG, plus Brazil (+1,410% only because of the six-week base). FY28E +14% and FY29E +12% as KTM rebuilds dealer stock-normalised volumes (2023 revenue was EUR2.66 bn).
segments._marginWhy: This line's EBITDA was -Rs744 cr in FY26 (KTM's first six weeks: inventory at fair value, restructuring costs) and +Rs322 cr (9.7%) in Q1FY27. Bajaj Mobility's own IFRS EBITDA margin was 1.7% in Q1 2026 and 8.7% in Q2 2026; KTM earned 12-16% in 2021-2023. 9% / 10% / 11%: the turnaround continues but we do not assume a return to pre-crisis margins within the forecast.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated (none: the three lines sum to reported EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Standalone + BACL + KTM/other subsidiaries & consolidation = consolidated revenue and EBITDA by construction (history in segments.json).

businessLines._why: Standalone revenue build. Domestic = units x domestic revenue per unit (sale of products less exports, so it includes domestic spares): FY26 Rs35,698 cr on 28.67 lakh units = Rs124,491. Exports = units x USD per unit x rupees per export dollar: FY26 $2,253 m (AR Table 4) on 22.50 lakh units = $1,001, and Rs20,416 cr / $2,253 m = Rs90.6. Other operating revenue (export incentives Rs572 cr, PLI/PSI incentives Rs1,040 cr, royalty Rs496 cr, misc.): Rs2,619 cr in FY26 (AR note 23). FY27E volumes = Apr-Aug 2026 actual + Sep-Mar at the growth shown on the Sep-Mar FY26 base. Checked against model revenue in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js.

standalone._why: Below-EBITDA lines used to turn the standalone segment into standalone EPS for the P/E part of the SOTP (BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js). Depreciation Rs400 cr (FY25), Rs448 cr (FY26), Rs118 cr in Q1FY27; capacity to rise from 7 mn to 9 mn units (EVs, premium bikes, 3W). Interest Rs36 cr (FY26), Rs4 cr in Q1FY27. Other income = the model's treasury-income line (surplus funds at the yield below; FY26 standalone other income Rs1,532 cr, Q1FY27 Rs512 cr; brokers model Rs1,610-1,820 cr for FY27E after ~Rs9,825 cr paid out in July 2026). Tax 25.2% (Q1FY27 25.1%, FY26 24.8%).

assumptions._capexWhy: Consolidated capex Rs879 cr (FY25), Rs694 cr (FY26; standalone ~Rs500 cr, split equally ICE and EV). FY27-29E: standalone ~Rs900-1,000 cr a year for the 7 mn -> 9 mn unit capacity expansion (EV 2W/3W, premium motorcycles, 3W) plus KTM ~EUR100 m a year (EUR73 m in restructuring-year 2025, EUR178-284 m in 2021-2024) plus BACL ~Rs20 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: Consolidated depreciation Rs645 cr in FY26 (KTM for six weeks) and Rs405 cr in Q1FY27 (Rs1,620 cr annualised: standalone Rs118 cr, BACL ~Rs3 cr, KTM and others ~Rs284 cr incl. amortisation of the Rs3,925 cr of KTM brand and technology intangibles recognised at acquisition). Gross block Rs15,919 cr at Mar-26 incl. KTM at fair value. 9.5% of average gross block gives ~Rs1,610 cr in FY27E.

operatingDebt._why: BACL's borrowings in the consolidated balance sheet at Mar-26: secured INR term loans Rs13,133 cr, ECB Rs2,409 cr, NCDs Rs500 cr, accrued interest Rs26 cr (AR FY26 consolidated note 16; financing-segment liabilities Rs16,003 cr, note 44). They fund the loan book, so they are working capital of the lending business, not group debt; KTM's bank loans (~Rs6,230 cr incl. the EUR473 m drawn under the EUR550 m facility), leases and sales-tax deferral stay as debt.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to consolidated cash and investments less non-BACL borrowings: Rs21,069 cr at Mar-26 (cash Rs3,072 cr + investments Rs24,642 cr - borrowings Rs22,713 cr incl. leases + BACL borrowings Rs16,068 cr). 8.1% x Rs21,069 cr = Rs1,707 cr in FY27E, in line with standalone other income of Rs1,532 cr in FY26 and Rs512 cr in Q1FY27 and brokers' Rs1,610-1,820 cr for FY27E. The yield looks high because the base is net of KTM's debt, whose interest is charged separately below (engine workaround, as for ASIANPAINT).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income of the subsidiaries: consolidated other income exceeded standalone by Rs176 cr in Q1FY27 (KTM, Brazil, BAIH BV interest after KTM repaid its loans in Feb-2026). FY26 reported other income was Rs2,182 cr plus Rs561 cr share of KTM as an associate (incl. Rs1,599 cr one-off remeasurement and currency-reserve gains) less Rs39 cr exceptional items; BAIH BV's interest on its loans to KTM stopped when KTM refinanced in Feb-2026. Consolidated FY27E other income ~Rs2,100 cr vs Rs2,146 cr in FY26 before the associate and exceptional items.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (KTM bank debt, leases; BACL's funding cost is in EBITDA)
assumptions._interestWhy: Consolidated finance cost Rs1,169 cr in FY26, of which BACL Rs908 cr (moved into BACL's EBITDA) and Rs261 cr other; Q1FY27 Rs387 cr of which BACL ~Rs305 cr, leaving Rs82 cr (~Rs330 cr a year): KTM's EUR473 m drawn at EURIBOR+1.40% after the Feb-2026 refinancing, other KTM loans, leases. Falls as KTM repays from Jun-2027.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT Rs4,423 cr, attributable profit Rs3,226 cr -> 27.1% (tax 27.9% less a Rs37 cr minority share of KTM's loss). Standalone and BACL pay ~25.2%; KTM's losses carry little tax credit, and as KTM turns profitable the minorities take 25% of its profit. 26.5% / 26.0% / 25.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Cash returned to shareholders, incl. buybacks, as % of the year's profit (engine workaround: the engine pays out of the same year's profit). FY27: Rs9,825 cr paid in July 2026 = 100% of FY26 standalone profit (final dividend Rs150 a share, Rs4,192 cr, plus a Rs5,633 cr tender buyback at Rs12,000), ~75% of our FY27E profit. FY28-29E 65%: Bajaj paid 70-90% of standalone profit in FY21-23 and 66-72% in FY25 (MOSL models 64-66%).

dcf._betaWhy: Two- and three-wheelers are cyclical and half the business is exported to emerging markets with volatile currencies; net cash and a strong balance sheet offset: beta 0.9, cost of equity 11.9%.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; two-wheeler demand is maturing in India (motorcycles grew ~4% a year over FY19-26) while exports and EVs add growth. 5.5%, the middle of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% over 15 years: ~4-5% volume plus ~3-4% price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~19.5% in FY29E (standalone 20.7%, BACL after funding cost, KTM ~11%) faded to 19%: competition in EVs and the end of PLI and currency tailwinds.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~1.9% to 2% of revenue (maintenance plus regular capacity).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Exports run at 250k+ a month and Nigeria and LatAm keep growing; the Pulsar refresh and two new 125cc brands win back domestic share; Chetak capacity unlocks and EVs stay at double-digit margins; standalone margin ~21.5%; KTM's turnaround reaches low-teens margins by FY29.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: An export market hits a currency crisis again (as Nigeria did in 2023-24), the rupee strengthens and commodity inflation persists; domestic share keeps slipping in the 100-125cc segments; standalone margin falls to ~19%; BACL's credit costs rise; KTM stalls near break-even.

sotp._why: Inputs for the SOTP in BAJAJ-AUTO.ctx.js. Core: standalone EPS (post-buyback count) x the derived P/E (own forward median on standalone EPS x the auto-sector de-rating), Sep-28E. BACL: peers' median P/B at 30-Sep-2026 (CHOLAFIN, SHRIRAMFIN, M&MFIN) on BACL's book at Sep-27E (the target date). KTM: 74.94% of Bajaj Mobility AG's market value on 30-Sep-2026 (EUR31.75, Vienna close; 33.797 mn shares; EUR/INR 109.19, FBIL 24-Sep-2026) less a holding discount (Anand Rathi uses 20%).
